title: Chicken & Lentil One-Pot

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g

steps: Heat the oil in the pot and cook the chicken for about 4 minutes, stirring.
Add the lentils, water, stock cube, paprika, cumin and pepper.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook for about 15 minutes, then add the frozen vegetables.
Continue cooking until the lentils are soft and the chicken is cooked through.
If it becomes too dry before the lentils are ready, add another ½ mug water.
notes: Red or green lentils work. Red lentils cook faster and make a softer, thicker dish; green lentils keep more texture and may need slightly more water.

title: Chicken, Tomato & Vegetable Stew

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g
Up to ½ mug water, only if needed
Up to 1 mug water, only if needed

steps: Heat the oil and cook the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and seasoning and stir briefly.
Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for about 10 minutes.
Add the frozen vegetables and cook for another 10–15 minutes, until the chicken and vegetables are cooked.
Add water only if the stew becomes too thick.
notes: Oregano can be used instead of paprika. Can be eaten alone or with a small amount of rice, pasta or potato.

title: Chicken & Chickpea Curry

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g
About 1 tbsp curry powder, then adjust

steps: Heat the oil and soften the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for about 4 minutes.
Add the curry powder and optional chilli and stir briefly.
Add the chopped tomatoes, chickpeas and frozen vegetables.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are tender.
If using yoghurt, remove from the heat and stir it in at the end.
notes: Rice is optional; the chickpeas already make this a substantial meal.

title: Lemon Garlic Chicken, Potatoes & Green Beans

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g

steps: Heat the oil in the pot and cook the chicken for 3–4 minutes.
Add the garlic and stir briefly.
Add the potatoes, water and stock cube.
Cover and cook for about 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and continue cooking until the potatoes, beans and chicken are cooked.
Stir in the lemon juice at the end.
Add a little more water during cooking if needed.
notes: Fresh or frozen green beans work.

title: Chicken & Spinach Yoghurt

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g
1 × 125 g pot Mythos Natural Greek yoghurt

steps: Heat the oil and cook the chicken until nearly cooked through.
Add the garlic, paprika and optional chilli.
Add the frozen spinach and cook until hot and most excess water has evaporated.
Remove from the heat and stir in the yoghurt.
Season with black pepper.
When reheating, heat gently rather than boiling the yoghurt sauce.
notes: Can be eaten alone or with a small amount of rice. This remains a recipe to evaluate after Maia has cooked it.

title: Chicken Noodle Bowl

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g

steps: Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions and drain.
Heat the oil in the 3 L pot and cook the chicken for about 4 minutes.
Add garlic and optional ginger/chilli.
Add the frozen Oriental vegetables.
Add 2 mugs water, 1 stock cube and the soy sauce.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook until the chicken and vegetables are done.
Add the cooked noodles, heat together for another minute and serve.

title: Creamy Tomato Spinach Pasta with Chicken

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g
250 g dry pasta — half a standard 500 g pack
100 ml cooking cream — half a 200 ml pack

steps: Cook the pasta until just tender and drain.
Heat the oil and cook the chicken.
Add the garlic and optional chilli.
Add the chopped tomatoes and spinach and simmer until the spinach is hot and the sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in the cooking cream.
Add the pasta and mix well.
Season with black pepper.
notes: For the large batch, use the 5 L pot. When reheating, add a small splash of water if the pasta has absorbed too much sauce. Freezing is possible, but the pasta texture is better fresh or refrigerated.

title: Chicken & Vegetable Stir-Fry

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g

steps: If using rice or noodles, cook them separately.
Heat the oil in the frying pan and cook the chicken until almost cooked.
Add garlic, optional ginger and chilli.
Add the frozen vegetables and cook until hot and the chicken is completely cooked.
Add the soy sauce and mix.
Serve alone or with the selected accompaniment.

title: Thai Green Chicken Curry

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g

steps: Heat the curry paste with a little oil for about 1 minute if needed.
Add the coconut milk, water and stock cube and bring gently to a simmer.
Add the chicken and green beans.
If using pumpkin, add small cubes early enough to cook through.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked and the beans are tender.
Add fish sauce at the end if using.
Taste and add more curry paste only if needed.
notes: This curry is intentionally very saucy. Fresh green beans are excellent; frozen green beans are also fine.

title: Asian Chicken & Edamame Rice Bowl

ingredients.display: ½ of a 700 g chicken breast pack — about 350 g
200 g shelled edamame — half a 400 g bag

steps: Cook the rice.
Heat the oil in the frying pan or 3 L non-stick pot and cook the chicken until almost done.
Add garlic and optional ginger/chilli.
Add the frozen vegetables and edamame.
Cook until everything is hot and the chicken is cooked through.
Add the soy sauce and serve over or mixed with the rice.
notes: Use the 3 L non-stick pot if the frying pan feels too crowded.

title: Turkey & Vegetable Rice Pot

ingredients.display: ½ of a ~500 g turkey strips pack — about 250 g

steps: Heat the oil in the pot and cook the turkey for 3–4 minutes.
Add the rice, frozen vegetables, water, stock cube, paprika and pepper.
Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer until the rice is cooked and the turkey is cooked through.
Check during cooking and add a small splash of water if needed.
Add chilli if wanted.

title: Turkey & Lentil Tomato Pot

ingredients.display: ½ of a ~500 g turkey pack — about 250 g

steps: Heat the oil and cook the turkey for about 3 minutes.
Add the lentils, chopped tomatoes, water, stock cube and paprika.
Bring to the boil, then simmer.
After about 10–15 minutes, add the frozen vegetables.
Continue cooking until the lentils are soft and the turkey is completely cooked.
Add another ½ mug water if the lentils need more liquid.
notes: Red or green lentils work; red lentils cook faster and thicken the pot more.

title: Turkey Stir-Fry

ingredients.display: ½ of a ~500 g turkey pack — about 250 g

steps: Cook the selected rice or noodles separately if using.
Heat the oil in the frying pan and cook the turkey until nearly done.
Add garlic and optional ginger/chilli.
Add the frozen vegetables and cook until hot and the turkey is fully cooked.
Add the soy sauce and mix.
Serve alone or with the selected accompaniment.

title: Turkey Jardineira
steps: Heat the oil in the 5 L pot and cook the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add the turkey and brown for about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and paprika and cook briefly.
Add the chopped tomatoes, water, stock cube and optional bay leaf.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for about 20 minutes.
Add the frozen Jardineira vegetables and continue cooking for another 15–20 minutes, until the turkey is tender and vegetables are cooked.
Add another ½ mug water if it becomes too dry.
Remove the bay leaf before serving.
notes: A beef Jardineira pack also works, but generally needs longer cooking.

title: Turkey Stroganoff with Mushrooms
steps: Use the 3 L non-stick pot or the 5 L pot.
Heat the oil and cook the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add the turkey and cook for about 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and garlic and cook until the mushrooms soften and most released liquid has reduced.
Add paprika and optional mustard.
Reduce the heat and stir in the cooking cream.
Cook gently for another 3–5 minutes until the turkey is cooked through.
Season with black pepper.
notes: Do not boil vigorously after adding the cream. Fresh or frozen mushrooms work.

title: Beef Bolognese

ingredients.display: ½ of a 465 g beef mince pack — about 230 g
250 g dry pasta — half a 500 g pack

steps: Cook the pasta separately and drain.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add the beef mince and break it up with a spoon until browned.
Add garlic and oregano.
Add chopped tomatoes and optional frozen vegetables.
Simmer for about 15–20 minutes.
Season with black pepper and serve with pasta.
notes: For a large batch, storing some sauce separately from the pasta improves reheating.

title: Beef & Black Bean Chilli

ingredients.display: ½ of a 465 g beef mince pack — about 230 g
1 × 420 g tin black beans — about 260 g drained
Up to ½ mug water if needed
1 × 820 g tin black beans — about 520 g drained
Up to 1 mug water if needed

steps: Heat the oil and soften the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add the beef and cook until browned.
Add garlic, paprika, cumin and chilli.
Add chopped tomatoes, drained black beans and vegetables.
Simmer for about 15–20 minutes.
Add water only if it becomes too thick.
notes: Black beans / feijão preto are Maia's default. Kidney beans or another cooked bean can substitute. Rice is optional.

title: Meatballs in Tomato Sauce

ingredients.display: ½ of a 465 g beef mince pack — about 230 g
Up to ½ mug water if using fresh tomatoes and needed
Up to ½ mug water if using fresh tomatoes and needed

steps: Mix the mince with the egg, breadcrumbs and black pepper.
Shape into small meatballs.
Heat the oil and brown the meatballs, turning to colour several sides.
Leave the meatballs in the pan, push them slightly aside and add the onion and garlic.
Cook for 2–3 minutes around the meatballs.
Add the selected tomatoes and oregano.
Cover and simmer gently for about 15–20 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through.
If using fresh tomatoes and the sauce becomes too dry, add a little water; if too wet, finish uncovered.
notes: Half batch makes roughly 8–10 small meatballs; full batch roughly 16–20. Plain Panko or flour also works if already available. For the full batch, use the 3 L non-stick pot after browning if the frying pan is too crowded.

title: Tuna & Vegetable Rice

ingredients.display: 1 large tuna tin — about 385 g / 270 g drained

steps: Put the rice, water and stock cube into the pot.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
When the rice is partly cooked, add the frozen vegetables.
Continue cooking until the rice and vegetables are ready, adding a small splash of water if needed.
Drain the tuna and fold it gently through.
Heat for another 2–3 minutes and add pepper and optional soy/chilli.

title: Tuna & Chickpea Tomato Pot

ingredients.display: 1 large tuna tin — about 385 g / 270 g drained
Up to ½ mug water if needed

steps: Heat the oil and cook the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add garlic, paprika and optional chilli.
Add the chopped tomatoes, chickpeas and selected vegetables.
Simmer for about 10–15 minutes.
Drain the tuna and add it near the end.
Mix gently and heat for another 2–3 minutes.
Add a little water only if the mixture becomes too thick.
notes: No rice is needed by default because the chickpeas make the dish filling.

title: Tuna, Egg & Chilli Fried Rice with Peas

ingredients.display: 1 small tuna tin — about 120 g / 85 g drained
1 fresh or frozen chilli, or to taste

steps: Cook the rice and let it cool a little if possible.
Heat the oil in the frying pan.
Add the peas and chilli and cook until hot.
Add the rice and stir.
Push everything to one side and scramble the eggs.
Mix the egg through the rice.
Drain the tuna and add it with the soy sauce.
Mix gently and heat through.
notes: Leftover cooked rice works particularly well.

title: Hake, Potato & Vegetable Pot

ingredients.display: 400–500 g frozen vegetables or green beans

steps: Put the potatoes, water and stock cube into the pot.
Bring to the boil, reduce the heat and cook for about 10 minutes.
Add the frozen vegetables.
Place the hake medallions on top and add garlic, paprika and pepper.
Cover and cook gently until the potatoes are tender and the hake is cooked through and flakes easily.
Avoid stirring vigorously once the fish is cooking.
Finish with lemon juice if wanted and add another ½ mug water if necessary.
notes: Recommended purchase: 400 g Medalhões de Pescada do Cabo Ultracongelados Continente. Follow the defrosting/cooking instructions on the pack.

title: Salmon & Veg Rice
steps: Cook the rice.
Heat the frozen vegetables.
Heat the oil in the frying pan and cook the salmon until cooked through and it flakes easily at the thickest part.
Serve each salmon portion with rice and vegetables.
Finish with the selected lemon or soy sauce if wanted.
notes: Follow the defrosting/cooking instructions on the salmon pack.

title: Salmon & Edamame Rice Bowl

ingredients.display: 200 g shelled edamame — half a 400 g bag

steps: Cook the rice.
Heat the edamame and Oriental vegetables together in the pot.
Heat the oil in the frying pan and cook the salmon until cooked through.
Add garlic and optional ginger/chilli to the vegetables.
Add soy sauce and mix.
Divide rice and vegetables between two bowls and place one salmon portion on each.
notes: Follow the salmon pack instructions. The remaining half of the edamame bag stays frozen for another recipe.

title: Chickpea & Spinach Curry

ingredients.display: 1 × 540 g tin chickpeas — about 400 g drained
½ of a 750 g bag frozen spinach
2 × 540 g tins chickpeas — about 800 g drained

steps: Heat the oil and cook the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add garlic, curry powder and optional chilli and stir briefly.
Add chopped tomatoes, drained chickpeas, frozen spinach and water.
Cover and cook gently until the spinach has defrosted.
Stir everything together and simmer uncovered for another 5–10 minutes until the sauce reaches the preferred thickness.
notes: Rice is optional. A spoonful of Mythos yoghurt can be added to individual servings if wanted.

title: Black Bean & Vegetable One-Pot

ingredients.display: 1 × 420 g tin cooked black beans — about 260 g drained
1 × 820 g tin black beans — about 520 g drained

steps: Heat the oil and cook the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add garlic, paprika, cumin and optional chilli.
Add chopped tomatoes, drained black beans, frozen vegetables, water and stock cube.
Simmer for about 15 minutes until the vegetables are cooked and the sauce has thickened.
notes: Black beans / feijão preto are Maia's default. Kidney beans, mixed beans or another cooked bean can substitute.

title: Lentil Vegetable Stew
steps: Rinse the selected lentils.
Put the lentils, chopped tomatoes, frozen vegetables, seasoning, water and stock into the pot.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Red lentils cook faster and thicken the stew; green lentils take longer and keep more texture.
Add another ½ mug water if needed before the lentils are tender.
Season with black pepper.

title: Sopa de Lentejas
steps: Prepare the lentils according to their packet instructions if they require soaking.
Put lentils, onion, garlic, carrots, water, stock cubes and cumin into the pot.
Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently.
Once the lentils start to soften, add the potatoes.
Continue cooking until the lentils, carrots and potatoes are tender.
Add another ½–1 mug water if the soup becomes too thick.
Add coriander at the end if wanted and season with pepper.
notes: This is deliberately different from the quick Lentil Vegetable Stew.

title: Lentil Bolognese

ingredients.display: 250 g dry pasta — half a 500 g pack

steps: Heat the oil and cook the onion for 2–3 minutes.
Add garlic and oregano.
Add red lentils, chopped tomatoes, water and stock cube.
Add the optional frozen vegetables if using.
Simmer until the lentils are soft and the sauce is thick, adding another ½ mug water if needed.
Cook the pasta separately and serve with the lentil sauce.
notes: Store some pasta separately from the sauce if making the large batch; it reheats better.

title: Chickpea Stir-Fry

ingredients.display: 1 × 540 g tin chickpeas — about 400 g drained

steps: Drain the chickpeas well.
Heat the oil in the frying pan.
Add the chickpeas and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Add the frozen Oriental vegetables, garlic and optional ginger/chilli.
Cook until the vegetables are hot and excess water has evaporated.
Add the soy sauce and serve alone or with optional rice.

title: Spanish Tortilla + Vegetables

ingredients.display: 300–400 g vegetables or salad to serve

steps: Cut the potatoes into small thin pieces and slice the onion if using.
Heat the oil in the 24 cm frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add the potatoes and onion, cover and cook gently until the potatoes are completely tender but not crisp.
Beat the eggs with a little salt and pepper.
Mix the cooked potato mixture into the eggs.
Return everything to the frying pan and cook until the bottom and sides are set.
Place a large plate over the pan, carefully turn the tortilla onto the plate, then slide it back into the pan.
Cook the second side until set to Maia's preferred level.
Serve hot, warm or cold with vegetables or salad.
notes: Sized for Maia's 24 cm frying pan.

title: Egg Fried Rice
steps: Cook the rice and ideally allow it to cool before frying.
Heat the oil in the frying pan.
Add the frozen vegetables and cook until hot.
Add the rice and stir-fry for a few minutes.
Push rice and vegetables to one side and scramble the eggs.
Mix everything together, add soy sauce and optional chilli, and cook for another minute.
notes: Leftover cooked rice works particularly well.

title: Chicken Salad Bowl

ingredients.display: About 200–250 g cooked chicken, preferably leftover
Juice of ½ lemon or a little vinegar

steps: Slice or dice the cooked chicken.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes.
Mix the salad leaves and vegetables.
Add the chicken and dress with lemon or vinegar, olive oil and black pepper.
notes: Designed primarily to use leftover chicken. If selected without leftovers, its chicken quantity still contributes to the weekly chicken requirement.

title: Chicken Wraps
steps: Slice the cooked chicken.
Lay out the wraps and add salad, cucumber and tomato.
Add the chicken and yoghurt.
Add pepper and optional chilli, then roll tightly.

title: Tuna Salad Bowl

ingredients.display: 2 × small 120 g tuna tins — about 85 g drained each
Juice of ½ lemon or a little vinegar

steps: Drain the tuna.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes.
Mix the vegetables and olives.
Add the tuna and dress with lemon or vinegar, olive oil and pepper.

title: Creamy Tuna Salad / Wrap Filling

ingredients.display: 1 × 125 g pot Mythos natural Greek yoghurt

steps: Drain the tuna and chop the cucumber finely.
Mix tuna, cucumber and yoghurt.
Add lemon juice and black pepper.
Add optional chilli.
Eat as a salad or use as wrap filling.
notes: Using one whole 125 g yoghurt pot avoids leaving half an opened pot.

title: Cold Egg & Vegetable Bowl

ingredients.display: About 300 g cooked and cooled vegetables

steps: Boil the eggs until cooked to Maia's preference.
Cool, peel and cut them into halves or quarters.
Prepare the selected vegetables.
Divide between two bowls and add two eggs to each.
Dress with a little olive oil, lemon or vinegar and pepper.

title: Egg Wraps
steps: Beat the eggs with black pepper.
Scramble them gently in the frying pan.
Divide between two wraps.
Add salad or spinach and tomato.
Add optional chilli, cheese or yoghurt, then roll and serve.

title: Chickpea Salad

ingredients.display: 1 × 540 g tin chickpeas — about 400 g drained

steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes.
Mix everything together.
Add lemon juice, olive oil and black pepper.
Add any optional vegetables.

title: Lentil Cold Salad

ingredients.display: 1 pack cooked lentils — 3 × 130 g drained portions
Juice of ½ lemon or vinegar

steps: Open and drain the cooked lentils if necessary.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes.
Mix everything together.
Add lemon or vinegar, olive oil and pepper.
Chill until needed.
notes: If Maia already has leftover cooked lentils, use those instead.

title: Simple Leftover Rice Salad

batchOptions.label: One batch
notes: Use about 1–1½ mugs of whatever suitable vegetables are already available.

steps: Use properly chilled leftover cooked rice.
Choose one protein.
Add whatever suitable vegetables are available.
Mix everything together and add the dressing.
Keep chilled until eaten.
notes: This recipe exists specifically to use leftovers; it should not create new shopping requirements for the rice, chosen protein or flexible vegetables unless the user explicitly decides otherwise.

title: Sardine Salad Bowl
steps: Open the sardines and drain slightly if needed.
Chop the vegetables.
Divide vegetables between two bowls.
Add one tin of sardines to each portion.
Add lemon or vinegar and pepper.
notes: No additional oil is usually necessary if the sardines are packed in olive oil. This recipe is provisional and can be removed later if Maia never chooses it.

title: Vietnamese-Style Chicken Rice-Paper Rolls
steps: Cook the rice noodles according to the packet instructions, drain and cool.
Cook the edamame if required by the packet, then cool.
Prepare the chicken, cucumber and carrot before rolling.
Put warm water into a wide plate or shallow bowl.
Dip one rice-paper wrapper briefly in the water until flexible.
Place it on a plate or board.
Put a small amount of noodles, chicken, cucumber, carrot and edamame across the lower-middle.
Fold the bottom over the filling, fold in the sides, then roll tightly.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers.
Mix the dipping-sauce ingredients together.
notes: Do not overfill the wrappers. Chicken is used rather than prawns. If the rolls prove fiddly, the same ingredients can be eaten as a noodle bowl.
